text:
Brandon Hagel was the Lightning's best player in October by the team's own vote, and the underlying numbers agree. Tampa gets 62% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, his own chances (10.5 expected goals) lead a lot of the league, and Evolving-Hockey had his team creating 0.44 more expected goals per 60 with him out there last season, 99th percentile among forwards. He also made headlines this month for remarks read as a jab at Dylan Larkin in the middle of the Nikita Kucherov trade saga.

The points have lagged the process. The Lightning have scored 9.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with Hagel on the ice, and his nine goals sit a little below his expected total. That kind of on-ice bad luck usually turns. The one odd note: his ice time is down more than two minutes a night over his last ten games.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him both a setup man and a player who gets to the slot. Our projection lands him around 84 points; we think that's reachable.
headline: Hagel is owed goals, and minutes
